title: With Cache Components in a PRODUCTION build, a synchronous fs read freezes into the static shell
statement: With cacheComponents enabled, under `next build` followed by `next start`, a Server Component reading an artifact with fs.readFileSync produces output baked into the static shell, so a later external write does not change what a fresh request returns.
notes: Carved out of AST-0007 after the dev refutation. This is what the documentation actually describes, and it is untested. ⚠️ It may never matter: #2 and #22 make the app local-only, so `next dev` may be the only mode this product ever runs in — which is itself a decision nobody has taken. ⚠️ REGISTERED VALIDATION TASK, DEFERRED 2026-08-22 under #80 branch 3 — not an outstanding debt. DEC-0001 makes this blocking only when a production build enters scope, and the product is local and runs `next dev`. Validating it now would test an UNDECLARED deployment mode: demand-driven sequencing means the experiment arrives with the commitment that needs it. REOPENING CONDITION: execute before adopting `next build` / `next start`, or when upgrading beyond the currently tested Next.js version (16.3.1 / React 19.2.8 / Node v24.18.0). ⚠️ The condition fires when the risk becomes POSSIBLE, not when it is observed — #80's stated preference, because the second means shipping the failure once to learn it was real. ⚠️ REOPENED 2026-08-25 — THE CONDITION FIRED, AND ON BOTH CLAUSES. DEC-0018 adopts `next build` + `next start` as the shipped configuration, which is the first clause verbatim; and the version now in play is Next.js 16.3.2 (sourced 2026-08-24, installed by the watcher probe 2026-08-25) against a claim whose targetEnvironment names 16.3.1, which is the second. This is no longer a registered-and-deferred validation task: it is OWED, and it is owed before anything in the application shell rests on how a Server Component's artifact read behaves in production. ⚠️ It is owed at roadmap step 3b — stage 6, risk and feasibility — where the roadmap placed it when it was written, before this answer existed. ⚠️ Note what is still open inside it: the claim is conditional on `cacheComponents` being enabled, and whether the application enables it has not been decided. That is a scope question for the validation, not a reason to defer it again. ⚠️ RE-SCOPED 16.3.1 -> 16.3.2 ON 2026-08-25, and this is the reopening condition being EXECUTED rather than the target being fitted to a result. The condition's second clause was 'when upgrading beyond the currently tested Next.js version', so re-validating at the new version is the whole point of having written it; leaving the claim scoped to 16.3.1 would have made the fresh evidence inapplicable to it by construction. Every other dimension was MEASURED to be unchanged — React 19.2.8, Node v24.18.0, Windows, `next build` + `next start`, `fs.readFileSync` — so exactly one fact moved, and it is the one the condition named. ⚠️ VALIDATED 2026-08-25 (EVD-0022) — AND ITS CONDITIONAL FRAMING IS WRONG. The outcome holds: with cacheComponents enabled the value was baked into the build and three requests after an external write all served the stale value. But the disabled configuration behaved IDENTICALLY, so the freeze is not caused by Cache Components. See AST-0019. Anyone reading this assertion alone would conclude the risk can be mitigated by disabling the flag; it cannot. ⚠️ NOT OPERATIVE for design work (pm, 2026-08-25). AST-0019 is the claim to rest on. This one is retained as the narrower historically-motivated claim at rung 3: it is where the concern started, it is what the documentation described, and it is the record of a conditional framing that measurement corrected. Kept rather than retired, because deleting the claim that turned out to be too narrow would delete the reason anyone thought to test both configurations.
